searchText: *grumble* on both. 😢 I have a usecase for you: approve/permit The pattern occurs in probably the majority of Ethereum transactions, and self sponsorships would make it so we no longer need either. Approve is a horrible UX of ERC20 that *everyone* would love to get rid of and self sponsoring would achieve this goal. So I see this as *the most common* use case, not an uncommon one. Ooo, that's a good one. So instead of approving, you call into uniswap V4 with a TLP? TLP? The old name for the signed bundle sorry 😛 "transaction-like package" - back when it had gas/value/etc https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612 Yep I've used it (or something similar) with dai This pattern could be replaced *globally* with `AUTHORIZEDCALL`, but only if origin == sponsee are allowed. On top of that, we could allow single-transaction approve + call pattern, but again only if origin == sponsee is allowed. Who would act as the invoker though? Have some standard contract that calls approve? Some smart contract. Could be a globally shared one, or each dapp could build their own. That is a solvable problem though in either case. For sure I *believe* that those two use cases improve the user flow for the majority of transactions on Ethereum today. Users would no longer need to pre-approve all, for example. Which helps protect users. And transaction ordering and complications go away (e.g., stuck pending transactions). There is just sooo much good that comes of allowing origin == sponsee IMO that I am very reticent to disallow it. The one saving grace to your argument though is that we can always loosen constraints later pretty easily. Which is basically the same argument I was making for `require(value == 0)`. We can launch with that to "buy us time" to figure out the best path forward so we don't have to feel like we are rushing to make a decision. > sending value from the invoker has definite use cases Can you share or do you have these use cases written up? Only holding wrapped eth (or other ERC-20) and swapping it for the sponsee is the first that came to mind. You can definitely do it by sending it to the sponsee and then taking from their account. <@!543900561460822016> had another one IIRC I think in the case of WETH, it actually is *harder* to do it with invoker pays. Really? `AUTHCALL` to transfer to the invoker, unwrap, `AUTHCALL` with value? I guess you can just straight up unwrap in a single authcall. ``` // invoker pays authorize(signature) weth.transfer{type: authorizedcall}(this, amount) weth.withdraw(amount) target.method{type: authorizedcall, value: amount}() // sponsee pays authorize(signature) weth.withdraw{type: authorizedcall}(amount) target.method{type: authorizedcall, value: amount}() ```

```
// invoker pays
authorize(signature)
weth.transfer{type: authorizedcall}(this, amount)
weth.withdraw(amount)

weth.withdraw{type: authorizedcall}(amount)

```
